title_human: Chain D: proving the boundary-completed Franke/Layer-B theorem

claims.statement: For k>=3, Franke's weak functions have at most simple poles, so Res_{z=0}(z^{k-1} eta(z) omega-hat(z/tau)) = 0 automatically; consequently the paper's prior 'retain Franke's residue term' formulation (open Problem 5.3 in V8) was based on a wrong analytic completion, since the removable-singularity hypothesis only matters in weights 1,2.
claims.object: Franke critical-value theory / Layer-B boundary completion
claims.notes: Presented as a correction to the trunk's V8 paper; the thread explicitly says the earlier open problem asked for the wrong analytic completion.

claims.statement: Boundary-completed Franke-Layer-B theorem: given a finite-dimensional Eisenstein space E with Franke subspace E_F on which L = L_{S,k}: E_F -> C_crit is surjective, and any finite linear boundary map d: E -> B with K_crit := ker L, K_d := ker L ∩ ker d, B_var := d(K_crit), there is an exact sequence 0 -> K_d -> E -> P_d -> 0 with P_d := im(L,d) ⊆ C_crit ⊕ B, and a canonical exact sequence 0 -> B_var -> P_d -> C_crit -> 0. Choosing a right inverse s of L (L∘s = id) and defining the reduced boundary coordinate d_s(f) := d(f - s(Lf)) gives a split exact sequence 0 -> K_d -> E -> C_crit ⊕ B_var -> 0, with dim K_d = dim E - |S| - rank(d|_{K_crit}).
claims.object: Layer-B classification / Franke critical-boundary exact sequence
claims.notes: Full proof given by first-isomorphism-theorem + rank-nullity arguments in the thread; explicitly framed as replacing the previously open Layer-B problem from the trunk's V8 paper with a theorem.

claims.statement: For an Eisenstein basis element the cusp constant terms are explicit algebraic combinations of generalized Bernoulli values L(1-k, psi) = -B_{k,psi}/k (times Gauss/conductor factors), so the abstract boundary map d: E -> B can be represented by an explicit finite Bernoulli boundary matrix; concretely the level-100 computation used two 18x3 character-resolved cusp matrices of full rank with explicit nonzero minors.
claims.object: Bernoulli boundary matrix / level-100 Franke-eta example
claims.notes: Ties the abstract Layer-B theorem to the concrete level-100 numerical example already present (see trunk mention of the level-100 boundary experiment).

claims.statement: In the level-100 Franke-eta worked example, dim K_sc = 3, dim K_or = 1, dim K_d = 0, with the unique middle direction (1,-10,16) = (1-2V_2)(1-8V_2), and the full cusp matrix has rank 3 so no nonzero boundary-invisible direction remains -- i.e. the theoretical 3->1->0 kernel filtration matches the paper's exact cusp computation.
claims.notes: Presented as confirming the abstract theorem numerically/exactly, not merely as evidence for it.

claims.statement: For a primitive nonprincipal character chi of conductor f with chi(-1) = (-1)^k, the two standard Eisenstein orientations S_chi = E_{k,chi,1} and T_chi = E_{k,1,chi-bar} have constant terms a_infinity(S_chi)=0 while a_infinity(T_chi) = (1/2)L(1-k, chi-bar) != 0, and by Fricke a_0(T_chi)=0, a_0(S_chi) != 0, so the map {S_chi,T_chi} -> C^2 sending f to (a_infinity(f), a_0(f)) is an isomorphism -- i.e. the two opposite-parity principal-character regulator orientations lie outside Franke's 0,infinity-vanishing sector and are genuine boundary coordinate directions.
claims.object: principal-character Eisenstein orientations vs. Franke's nonprincipal critical sector
claims.notes: Uses standard Fourier/Atkin-Lehner theory for character Eisenstein newforms.

claims.statement: A follow-up 12-page standalone research report (BOUNDARY_COMPLETED_FRANKE_LAYERB_REPORT.pdf) restates the theorem as a split exact sequence 0 -> K_F -> E_F ⊕ P_chi -> C_crit ⊕ C^2 -> 0 after adjoining the two principal-character Eisenstein orientations as the missing boundary datum (rather than a surviving weak-function residue term), and additionally proves the kernel filtration K_{d,or} ⊆ K_or ⊆ K_sc, independence of the theorem from the chosen endpoint regularization on the principal-character plane, degeneracy/Hecke stability of Franke's critical-null kernel, and states a finite 'Franke-Bernoulli algorithm' (Franke/Vandermonde kernel -> orientation projectors -> cusp/Bernoulli matrix -> K_d).
claims.object: Boundary-completed Franke/Layer-B theorem, extended report version
claims.notes: Report claims to close the specific gap the trunk's Franke integration note had left open; a closed-form rank formula for the all-cusp Bernoulli matrix at general level/character is explicitly left open (see open_threads).

connections_to_literature: Franke's theory of critical-value kernels for Eisenstein series, including Theorem 2.11/2.13 on weak functions and the explicit weak-function/Vandermonde machinery for the critical kernel (arXiv, per-thread citation) — see trunk for the initial identification of this as the 'boundary-completed Franke picture' target
Standard Fourier-coefficient and Atkin-Lehner/Fricke theory for character Eisenstein series (pseudo-eigenvalues, constant terms at cusps)
open_threads_or_handoffs: No closed-form rank formula has been proved for the all-cusp Bernoulli boundary matrix at general level/character families (K_d's rank is computable algorithmically but not given a closed formula).
The precise motivic normalization comparing the modular constant-term/Bernoulli boundary coordinates with Eisenstein-symbol boundary residues is not established.

The thread flags that the foundational paper's (V8) discussion of Franke Theorem 2.11 needs correction: the residue term is not the relevant boundary phenomenon for k>=3 systems; this correction has not yet been confirmed as merged back into the main paper within this chain.
